title: Top Mistakes to Avoid in Property Development Finance
h1: Not revealed in search results. The SERP title 'Top Mistakes to Avoid in Property Development Finance' is most likely the HTML title tag; the on-page H1 could not be confirmed.
summary: Blog article from Silver Oak Capital titled 'Top Mistakes to Avoid in Property Development Finance' (slug: top-mistakes-to-avoid-when-applying-for-property-development-lending). Thesis: developers applying for property development lending make avoidable errors that weaken their application with lenders. Confirmed content: Mistake 1 - 'Underestimating Total Project Costs' (section heading confirmed in search b): described as 'perhaps one of the most common errors that developers make'; the cost estimate is both crucial to the success of the development and 'an important factor on which lenders base their lending decisions'; inaccurate figures make a developer look inexperienced; guidance is to factor in 'a healthy contingency (generally 5-15%)' to cover overruns, and for less experienced developers to consult architects and quantity surveyors. Mistake 2 (search a only, tool summary wording) - not having a clear exit strategy: lenders place great importance on the borrower's exit strategy because it determines when and how they are repaid. Search (b)'s tool summary added further Silver Oak points whose page attribution is uncertain (they may come from this article or from sibling Silver Oak articles returned alongside it): a weak exit - lenders want to see repayment via a sale with proven demand or a refinance onto a mortgage ('Borrowers generally rely on the sale or refinance of the development.'); inexperience - lenders prefer a strong track record and see first-time developers as higher risk ('Borrowers with limited experience or failed past projects are less likely to secure financing than experienced borrowers'); valuation and LTV - lenders commission a valuation of the current state of the site and apply a maximum day-one LTV, usually around 75% ('Lenders are constrained to a maximum day one loan to value (usually 75%)'); overstating GDV - explicitly attributed by the tool to the separate Silver Oak article 'Why 70% of London Development Finance Deals Get Rejected'. The full list of mistakes on the page was not revealed by either search.

sections.heading: Underestimating Total Project Costs
sections.content: Heading confirmed verbatim [b]. Failing to accurately estimate project costs is 'perhaps one of the most common errors that developers make' [a]. Cost estimation is 'crucial to the success of their development' and 'an important factor on which lenders base their lending decisions' [b]; lenders weigh it heavily [a]. Inaccurate figures make a developer look inexperienced [b]. Guidance: factor in 'a healthy contingency (generally 5-15%)' to cover overruns [a][b]; less experienced developers should consult architects and quantity surveyors [b].

sections.heading: Not having a clear exit strategy
sections.content: Heading wording taken from the search (a) tool summary; exact on-page heading not confirmed. Lenders place great importance on the borrower's exit strategy, as this will determine when and how they are repaid [a]. Search (b) adds (attribution uncertain): lenders want to see how the loan will be repaid, either through a sale with proven demand or a refinance onto a mortgage; 'Borrowers generally rely on the sale or refinance of the development.'

sections.heading: Further points surfaced in search (b) - page attribution uncertain
sections.content: Overstating gross development value (GDV): lenders base their terms on GDV; the tool attributed this point to the sibling article 'Why 70% of London Development Finance Deals Get Rejected'. Inexperience: lenders prefer developers with a strong track record and see first-time developers as higher risk; 'Borrowers with limited experience or failed past projects are less likely to secure financing than experienced borrowers'. Valuation and loan-to-value: lenders commission a valuation of the current state of the site and a maximum day-one LTV applies, 'usually 75%'. These may belong to this article or to /development-finance-requirements-in-the-uk-explained/ or /why-lenders-reject-70-of-london-resi-led-development-deals/, which were returned in the same search.

Its summary blended this article with sibling Silver Oak articles: only the title, the 'Underestimating Total Project Costs' heading and the two cost-estimation sentences are unambiguously from this URL; the GDV point was explicitly attributed to 'Why 70% of London Development Finance Deals Get Rejected'; the exit/inexperience/75% day-one LTV sentences could not be attributed to a specific page. The full list of mistakes on the page is unknown (likely more than two). H1, meta description, author, publication date, images, CTAs and FAQ were not revealed. Two Silver Oak URLs appeared that are not in seed.json: /complete-guide-to-development-loans-for-property-projects-uk/ and /why-lenders-reject-70-of-london-resi-led-development-deals/ (plus the AMP variant /regulating-bridging-loans-through-fca-rules/amp/ of a known article).
